calls.title: Variations in Phases
calls.summary: The team discussed strategies for managing experiment variations by implementing a just-in-time migration approach which allows midstream changes without disrupting existing data models. Stable REST API formats were emphasized to support external customers, with bespoke endpoints suggested for new actions. The importance of consistently maintaining variation weights, metadata duplication per phase, and using unique IDs for variations was highlighted to improve targeting and reduce bugs. The conversation also touched on converting simple boolean flags into a richer status model for variations, with a plan to address legacy experiments thoughtfully to minimize technical debt and analysis disruption. Overall, this meeting aimed to enhance the variation management framework while maintaining existing API integrity.
calls.keywords: Variations, Phases, Disabled Flag, Re-randomization, SDK Payload, API Compatibility
calls.action_items:
**Luke Sonnet**
Strip out front-end experimental code and prepare a PR that adds variations inside phases with just-in-time migration and no new functionality for initial review and testing (32:24)
Implement remove-variation workflows across different scenarios (same phase with disabled flag, new phase with re-randomization) in subsequent PRs after the initial migration (26:50)
Add a status enum field to variations to replace simple disabled boolean, preparing for richer status handling in future (32:37)

**Unassigned**
Ensure testing and validation of SDK payload changes particularly around targeting by variation key vs. index and handling reorders (17:55)
Monitor and plan for API backwards compatibility concerns due to moving variations under phases, possibly building bespoke endpoints or careful API mapping layers to avoid breaking external consumers (23:08)

**UI/UX team**
Disable editing of variations for old phases in the UI with appropriate tooltip messaging and ensure editing is only enabled on the latest phase (28:01)

**Luke, Bryce Fitzsimons, Adriel Vieira, and Michael Samper**
Follow up on deeper technical issues around inconsistent variation values across environments and SDK evaluation legacy quirks (19:40)
